value.summary: On rack R01, cable C05 was not fully clicked in; the tech reseated it by hand and the link came up.
On rack R01, the connector at C31 was not latched; the tech noted this was the second such case today.
On rack R01, the robot landed cable F22 in port FE-LEAF2/5 instead of FE-LEAF2/4, and it was moved to the correct port.
On rack R02, the robot had a gripper fault on C27 and stopped after three retries, and the tech finished the connection by hand.
On rack R04 at position C19, the robot's gripper dropped an RJ45 cable under the tray, and the tech retrieved it and plugged it in by hand.
On rack R01, the label on cable C40 read M2 while the port map says M1, and the tech printed a new label.

While the robot was routing cable C12 on rack R01, its arm caught the neighboring BMC cable, which was already up, and pulled it half out; the cable was reseated and the link came back after about 30 seconds.
On rack R09, the robot took about 4 minutes on cable C47 as its arm kept re-planning around the cable bundle, but it finished without tech help.
On rack R06 the robot's camera lost the port on F31 twice under the aisle LEDs, and the third try worked.
On rack R05, the cable tag F28 was printed for port P1 but the cable was on port P2, and the tech swapped the tags.
On rack R01, fiber F03 failed end face inspection, was cleaned, and passed a second inspection.
On rack R01, the fiber end face on F17 had dust on the ferrule, and the tech noted these jumpers came out of the bag without caps.
On rack R02, cable F09 had a kinked jacket right behind the connector, and the tech replaced it with a new jumper from spares.
The cable kit for rack R03 was missing two copper patch cords, which were pulled from spares with a 15-minute wait.
The rear door on rack R06 was locked, and the tech waited 20 minutes for a security badge.
A laptop cart left in the aisle blocked the robot at rack R08, and it waited about 4 minutes until the cart was moved; nobody was near the robot.
On rack R05, the 0.5 m cord for C33 was too short to reach the management switch without strain; a 1 m cord is needed.
On rack R06, cable F14 was found bent past its bend radius near the connector boot, and it was already in that condition when taken out of the bundle.
Tray 9 was not yet installed in rack R08 when the robot arrived, so the robot skipped those slots and returned to them after the tray was installed.
F30 on rack R02 had no link because the port map had P1 and P2 swapped for tray 15; the robot had followed the map correctly, and after the network team fixed the map the robot re-ran the connection.
On rack R08, the leaf switch port for F35 was administratively down; the network team enabled it and the link came up.
On rack R03, the MGMT-SW2 uplink was not yet patched at shift start, and the network team finished it before the robot reached those ports.
On rack R04, the port map revision on the tablet (rev C) and the rack sheet (rev D) disagreed for FE-LEAF2, so the fiber was held until the network team confirmed rev D.
A contractor walked into the aisle behind rack R02 while the robot arm was extended; the robot stopped within a second and resumed once he left, with no contact.
On rack R03, the robot's arm swung toward the tech's hand as they reached in to clear a zip tie, and the tech pressed the e-stop; the arm came close but did not touch them.
At rack R04, the robot pinched the tech's glove on the fiber tray door while the tech was holding the door open; there was no injury and the glove was not damaged.
An electrician working on the PDU in this row pressed the stop as a precaution while he opened the panel; it was not about the robot.
On shift 9 at rack R09, the tech noted something was off with the fiber and referred questions to Dana.
On rack R11 during shift 11, a few ports were flapping after lunch, and the tech was not sure whether the robot work or the switch was the cause.
On shift 13 at rack R13, the tech stepped in and left a note referring only to a photo, with no description of what happened.
